title: Emit audit events during Private install/upgrade/rollback/config apply
author: Amina Yusuf
description: Context: Private customers reported gaps in audit coverage for operator-driven installer actions (notably upgrades and RBAC-related config applies) and Security needs parity with Hosted/Dedicated for “sensitive actions.” This PR instruments the Private installer to emit audit events for install/upgrade/rollback/config-apply/credential-rotation flows using the audit schema v1 envelope and event_type taxonomy. Summary of changes: (1) Add an audit emitter to the installer runtime that writes v1-shaped events to the local audit spool and forwards to the cluster audit ingestion endpoint when configured. (2) Emit events at the start + completion of sensitive workflows with consistent correlation (admin_action_id) and stable event_id for dedupe. (3) Capture operator identity where available (kubeconfig user / OIDC subject / OS user) without logging secrets. (4) Include deployment context: private_installation_id, cluster_id (if known), namespace, installer_version, and target version for upgrades. Event types added: private.install.start, private.install.complete, private.upgrade.start, private.upgrade.complete, private.rollback.start, private.rollback.complete, private.config.apply, private.credential.rotate. Field behavior: schema_version is set to 1.0; actor.type is “human” when we can resolve a non-empty operator identity and “system” when running unattended; actor.id is set to a stable string (OIDC sub preferred; else kubeconfig user; else local OS username) and actor.display_name is best-effort. source.ip is best-effort (only when invoked via the controller/remote runner, not local CLI). target.type is “private_installation”; target.id is the private_installation_id. changes.summary includes a capped diff summary (max 1KB) for config apply and upgrade plan; raw manifests are never logged. Delivery semantics: best-effort to remote audit sink; guaranteed local spool write unless disk is full. On sink failure, the installer continues and records audit_sink_status=degraded in the event outcome.reason. Tests: add unit tests for event shape validation + redaction, plus an integration test that runs an upgrade dry-run in CI and asserts emitted events match the required fields list. Notes: This is aligned with ENG-4826 and the schema enforcement work in ENG-4821/ENG-4830; exporter normalization (schema_version tagging) remains in audit-log-exporter PRs but this PR ensures producers already emit correctly shaped v1 events. Follow-ups: add operator identity support for air-gapped installs using explicit --operator-id flag (tracked separately), and wire installer audit spool rotation metrics into the Private observability pack.

review_conversation: Kevin Osei: Can we guarantee schema_version is always present even in spool-only mode? Also please add event_id generation rationale (ULID vs UUID) in docs.
Amina Yusuf: Yes—schema_version is set in the envelope builder before any sink interaction. Added docs note: ULID chosen for time-sort + SIEM friendliness; event_id stable per action attempt.
Hanae Suzuki: Redaction looks good, but please ensure we never log kubeconfig raw bytes or token prefixes in changes.summary. Add a regression test for the near-miss pattern ("Bearer ").
Amina Yusuf: Added denylist patterns for "Bearer ", "client-certificate-data", "client-key-data" and a unit test that fails if any appear in the serialized event.
Sean Gallagher: What happens if spool write fails (disk full)? We should be explicit: does the installer fail the workflow or proceed? Also add a metric/log line so support can diagnose.

Amina Yusuf: Proceeding with workflow (best-effort audit) but we now print a structured error line and set outcome.reason=audit_spool_write_failed when we can still emit to sink; if both fail, we log a single-line warning with action_id + failure cause.
Connor O'Brien: Please confirm these event_type names match the centralized registry. If the exporter expects different names, we’ll create churn for customers.
Amina Yusuf: Synced names with the taxonomy draft used in ENG-4826; Kevin confirmed they align with exporter normalization rules. Added a comment in docs pointing to the registry source of truth.
Vivek Kulkarni: For customer comms, can we avoid implying guaranteed remote delivery? Wording should be “best-effort remote + local spool when enabled.”
Amina Yusuf: Updated docs and PR description to match delivery semantics language used in the ADR draft.
release_notes: Private installer now emits v1 audit events for install/upgrade/rollback/config apply/credential rotation workflows, including operator identity where available. Events are spooled locally and forwarded to the configured audit ingestion endpoint on a best-effort basis; secrets are redacted by default.
security_notes: Do not log secrets: kubeconfig contents, bearer tokens, client key material, and raw manifests are explicitly excluded/redacted. changes.summary is truncated and denylisted to prevent high-risk leakage and high cardinality.
qa_notes: Validated against golden fixtures; ran upgrade integration test in CI; manually verified spool rotation on repeated config.apply actions.
